question: The Annapurna Scheme was launched by the Government of India in the year ________ for providing food security.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Annapurna Scheme was launched in the year **2000** by the Government of India.

• The scheme aims to provide food security to **senior citizens** who are not covered under the National Old Age Pension Scheme (NOAPS).

• Under this scheme, eligible beneficiaries are provided with **10 kg of free rice** or wheat per month.

• The scheme is implemented by the **Ministry of Rural Development** in collaboration with the state governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Annapurna Scheme**

• The Annapurna Scheme was launched to provide food security to senior citizens who were not receiving benefits from the National Old Age Pension Scheme (NOAPS).

• The target group for the scheme is **senior citizens aged 65 years and above**.

• Each eligible beneficiary receives 10 kg of free rice or wheat per month under the scheme.

• The scheme is an important initiative to address the nutritional needs of vulnerable senior citizens and ensure their well-being.

• **National Old Age Pension Scheme (NOAPS)**

• NOAPS is a social security scheme designed to provide financial assistance to elderly individuals who are below the poverty line.

• Under NOAPS, eligible beneficiaries receive a monthly pension to support their basic needs.

• The scheme is part of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) and is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.

• NOAPS aims to ensure that elderly individuals have a source of income to maintain their dignity and quality of life.

• **Ministry of Rural Development**

• The Ministry of Rural Development is responsible for the implementation of various schemes aimed at poverty alleviation and rural development in India.

• The ministry works in collaboration with state governments to ensure effective implementation of these schemes.

• Some of the key schemes implemented by the ministry include the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G), and the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP).

• The ministry plays a crucial role in improving the socio-economic conditions of rural populations and promoting inclusive growth.
